requirement: All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
rationale:
**Obligations from `requirements.authoring.source_tools`:**
1. Assessments use the SDK graph and source tools.
2. A read uses the node address under `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`.
3. A delivered read records the node's fingerprint under `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
4. The source project follows `requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.

**Coverage:**
- **Tool set.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` asserts the exact sorted tool list sent to the model. It contains `read_node`, `outgoing_edges`, `outline_source`, `list_sources`, `search_text`, `search_structure`, `lookup_requirements`, `run_named_query`, `get_next_page`, `finish_search`, `github` and `submit_result`. It also checks that `read_node` accepts `path`, `location`, `node` and `data`. A read with `path` and `location` is delivered, and its text contains the file and content. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/search.rs#mod[tests]/fn[byte_search_reports_case_sensitive_one_based_matching_lines]` covers the text-search engine. `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` checks that a real model uses a read or search tool, and that the recorded input has the file, item and hash.
- **Read addressing.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` reads by `path` and `location`, and by a `Definition` data address. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` covers a malformed node (`invalid node ID`) and a missing file.
- **Fingerprint recorded on delivery.**
  - `citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads` asserts the recorded inputs contain `fn[first]`, `fn[second]` and the `terms.unused` definition text, and do not contain the unread `fn[untouched]`.
  - `explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues` asserts that failed or denied reads add nothing to the evidence.
  - The delivery-versus-prepared semantics, including a failed provider response recording nothing, are tested by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]`. That test is marked for `read_node.inputs` and `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. It belongs to the cited requirement, so I did not reassess it.
- **Local provider scope.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` runs with and without a Git repository. It covers nested `.gitignore` files and their exceptions, and untracked files being available. It covers ignored files, even ones Git tracks, being excluded from list, read, parse and text search, including when a file or subdirectory is named directly. It covers `.git` and `..` being excluded, and a direct read of an excluded file returning an error.
  - `explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues` checks the same scope through the agent tools. A direct read of an ignored file returns an error mentioning `excluded` with no content, and `list_sources` omits ignored files. `search_text` and `search_structure` return empty matches, and none of the ignored content leaks into the evidence.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` covers untracked files being available.

Every obligation has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome. The tests I looked at are marked. I found no marking gap and no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} source_tools

All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
:::{req} read_node.mcp
Give `read_node` a node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. The result contains the node’s text. If more
text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.
```text
read_node(NodeAddress) -> {text: string, next?: UUID}
// For a source node the result has these additional fields:
{file: string, selector: string, children: {node: NodeId, file: string, selector: string, header?: string}[]}
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{req} local_provider
Source inspection uses the project directory and respects `.gitignore`,
including nested ignore files and their exceptions. Untracked files are
available unless ignored. The same scope applies to listing, reading,
outlining, text search, and structural search, including requests naming a
file or subdirectory directly.
Files outside the project directory and Git metadata are excluded. A direct
read of an excluded file returns an error.
